subject: Action: sample prompts, edge-case taxonomy, and redaction guidance

Subject: Follow-up from demo — request for prompt inventory and redaction guidance

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today — the latency numbers looked promising and the live demo helped our product team picture how inference would slot into our triage flow. A couple of asks we discussed that I wanted to put in writing so we can track next steps: 

1) Prompt inventory template — our engineers and clinical SMEs will extract a representative set of prompts (patient-facing triage, clinician summarization, classification rules). Can you send a template for capturing sample prompts + context, expected output types, and any edge-case flags?

2) Redaction guidance — we need concrete rules for PHI removal prior to sending prompts to hosted inference. High level is fine, but please call out recommended redaction granularity, examples that break redaction, and any client-side scripts you recommend. Our security/legal team (cc'd) want to review.

3) Model guidance & benchmarks — would like suggested model families for a cost/latency/accuracy tradeoff and any benchmark artifacts for similar healthcare use-cases.

We can share an initial CSV of ~200 sample prompts by EOD Thursday if that aligns with your intake plan. Also open to a short runbook or MAP we can follow so we don't miss anything.

Thanks,
Sara
Senior PM, NovusHealth

Sara — thanks for the clear recap, and glad the demo was useful. Great to see legal already on the thread. Next steps from our side:

- I attached a lightweight prompt inventory template (redwood_prompt_template.csv) — it has columns for: prompt_text, role (user/system), expected_output_format, failure_mode_flag, privacy_flag (PHI/PII/none), and example edge-case notes. If you prefer JSON export we can accept that too.

- For redaction, I attached a one-pager summarizing our recommended client-side redaction approach (redaction-guidance-onepager.pdf). Short summary: remove direct identifiers (names, SSNs, MRNs), replace with structured placeholders (e.g., <PATIENT_NAME>), and keep clinical context that is necessary for the model to answer (e.g., symptoms, vitals). We include specific regex examples and a suggested lightweight JS/Python redaction snippet.

- Model guidance: initial suggestion for a triage pipeline (fast tier + accuracy tier):
  • Fast / low-cost: redwood-llama-13b-q4f — good for high throughput triage lists where latency is critical.
  • Mid / balanced: redwood-vicuna-13b-refine — better on instruction following and structured outputs.
  • High-accuracy / fallback: redwood-70b-refine-q8 — use for clinician-facing summaries where correctness matters.

Rishi (cc) will drop in the benchmark links and a short eval checklist we recommend for healthcare prompts.

Proposed MAP: you share the initial prompt CSV by Thu EOD -> we run a short quality sweep and map to model tiers -> we deliver a small eval report + suggested sample prompts to prioritize for fine-tuning or system prompt tuning. Target: turnaround 5 business days from receipt of CSV. If that works reply with confirmation and whether you want the hosted API or a Dedicated POC for the initial evaluation.

Thanks — I’ll hold on intake until your CSV.

—Marissa

Sara — adding a few technical notes and links so your engineers and security folks have concrete artifacts.

1) Benchmarks & evals
  • Healthcare prompt eval (our internal): https://redwood-internal.s3/benchmarks/2027/healthcare-novus-benchmarks.pdf (contains latency-by-model, token-cost estimates at 512/1024 seq lengths, and a small accuracy matrix on clinical summarization tasks).
  • Public ML perf notes: https://docs.redwood.com/model-catalog/perf-guides (recommend reviewing the sequence-length guidance).

2) Prompt collection tips (short):
  • Capture the minimal context the model needs — often removing extraneous PII increases accuracy because the model isn't distracted by irrelevant names/IDs.
  • Flag examples that require lookups (EHR-referenced data) — those typically need a retrieval step rather than straight LLM completion.
  • Include a few adversarial / malformed examples (abbreviations, misspellings, pasted PDFs) so we can test robustness.

3) Redaction specifics
  • Always mask direct identifiers with canonical placeholders (e.g., <PATIENT_DOB>, <MRN>). Avoid free-text redactions like "[redacted]" where possible — placeholders preserve structure.
  • For clinical notes, keep temporal and measurement info (e.g., "fever x3 days", vitals) but remove the exact name/ID tokens.
  • We recommend a two-pass approach: first client-side deterministic regex + dictionary redaction, then server-side light heuristic check (if you use hosted API). We can provide a runnable Python redaction utility as a starter.

4) Quick model-fit guidance (tradeoffs):
  • If throughput is >=200 req/s choose q4 quant variants for cost savings.
  • For structured JSON outputs we recommend models with instruction-tuning and a short system prompt that enforces JSON schema. We have a sample system prompt in the template.

If you want, we can include a small evaluation harness (pytest-style) that runs your CSV through 3 models and returns a triage-quality score and token-cost estimate. Happy to spin that up once we have your sample set.

-Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Marissa / Rishi — this is great, thanks for the concrete artifacts. Confirming we will: 

• Share a first pass CSV (~180 rows) by Thu EOD with a mix of patient questions, clinician notes to summarize, and a set of edge-case examples (abbreviations, OCR errors). File name will be novus_prompt_samples.csv.
• We prefer the hosted API for the initial eval (ease of onboarding) — please include token-cost estimates for 512/1024 tokens in the eval.
• Legal has a couple follow-ups on redaction: can you include the deterministic regexes used for names/SSNs in the one-pager (or the Python util) so we can validate them against our policies? Also want a note that logs will not retain raw prompt text if we ingest via the hosted API (we'll need your attestation language for SOC2 docs).

Can you confirm turnaround after we upload the CSV and whether the eval harness will produce CSV-level per-prompt scores? If yes, we'll proceed and book a 30-minute sync after the report is delivered to go over high-risk prompts.

Thanks,
Sara
